title: Select a subject and mask it
summary: Use Select Subject, turn the selection into a layer mask and refine it.

steps.say: In the Layers panel, click the photo layer so it is highlighted.

check.prompt: Is the layer that holds the photo highlighted in the Layers panel?

hints: It is usually the bottom row, named Background.
A lock on the Background layer is fine for this lesson.
steps.why: Selections and masks act on the highlighted layer.

steps.say: Open the Select menu at the top and choose Subject.

checks.prompt: Is there a moving dashed outline around the main subject of the photo?

hints: Give it a few seconds; Photoshop studies the photo before the outline appears.
With the Object Selection tool, key W, the options bar has a Select Subject button too.
steps.why: Select Subject finds the main person or object for you.

steps.say: Click Add layer mask at the bottom of the Layers panel. It looks like a rectangle with a circle.

check.prompt: Does the photo layer now have a second black and white thumbnail, with the background hidden?

hints: Or use Layer, then Layer Mask, then Reveal Selection.
Photoshop turns a locked Background into a normal layer when you add a mask.
steps.why: A mask hides the background without deleting any pixels.

steps.say: Click the black and white mask thumbnail so it gets a white frame.

check.prompt: Does the mask thumbnail in the Layers panel have a highlight frame around it?

hints: It is the second thumbnail on the photo layer's row.
If the frame is on the photo thumbnail instead, painting would change the photo.
steps.why: With the mask active, painting edits what is hidden or shown.

steps.say: Press B, then press X until white is the foreground color. Paint over any missing edges of the subject.

check.prompt: Has more of the subject been revealed than at the start of this step?

hints: White paint shows the layer, black paint hides it.
Use the bracket keys to change the brush size.
steps.why: Painting the mask lets you fix the automatic selection by hand.

steps.say: Hold Shift and click the mask thumbnail to switch the mask off.

check.prompt: Is a red cross shown over the mask thumbnail and the full photo visible again?

hints: Hold Shift first, then click once on the mask thumbnail.
Layer, then Layer Mask, then Disable does the same.
steps.why: Switching a mask off shows that nothing was deleted.

steps.say: Shift click the mask thumbnail again to switch it back on.

check.prompt: Is the background hidden again and the red cross gone from the mask thumbnail?

hints: Click the thumbnail with Shift held, the same way as before.
steps.why: The mask can be turned on and off or repainted at any time.
